newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy car market still ranked 2nd in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Italy car market still ranked 2nd in Europe.

text.p: Italy's car market, boosted by a government incentive scheme, remained in second place in Europe by size after Germany in March.

Italian carmakers' association Anfia said March new car registrations, up 25 percent year-on-year, confirmed the effects of the new cars for old scheme and put Italy in line to return to an annual sales volume of some two million vehicles.

New car sales were 220,500 in March, giving a cumulative total for the first three months of this year of 625,500. "With volumes like these the Italian market is reconfirmed as the second European market after Germany," Anfia said.

Car importing body Unrae also said the incentive scheme, introduced in January and set to run to end-September, had helped the domestic market recover after four depressed years but warned that "this measure alone will not be enough to resolve the structural problems of the sector."
The experience of other European markets, Unrae added, had shown that benefits deriving from incentive schemes should not be overestimated.
